title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 270
paragraphs: This I heard from the priests at Thebes, and what follows is said by the prophetesses of Dodona. They say that two black doves flew from Thebes in Egypt, one coming to Libya and the other to their land. The latter settled upon an oak-tree and spoke with human voice, saying that it was necessary a prophetic seat of Zeus should be established in that place; and they supposed that what was announced to them was of the gods, and accordingly made one. The dove that went away to the Libyans, they say, bade the Libyans make an Oracle of Ammon; and this also is of Zeus. The priestesses of Dodona told me these things — the eldest being named Promeneia, the next Timarete, and the youngest Nicandra; and the other people of Dodona who were engaged about the temple gave accounts agreeing with theirs.
